title: Chapter 2. Padas of the Puri Period
html:
Padas by contemporaries on the Lord's life in Puri after the sannyasa, in the order of events: the arrival in Nilachala and Sarvabhauma's house, the darshan of Jagannatha, sankirtana on the seashore, Radha's mood in the company of Svarupa Damodara and Ramananda Raya, the states of separation (dasha), the Gambhira, and the divine madness of prema (divya-unmada). Majumdar (*Sri-Chaitanya-chariter upadan, ch. 2) regards the Puri padas of Narahari Sarakara, Vasu Ghosha and Vasu Ramananda as the testimony of those who came to the Lord every year with the pilgrims from Gauda. The text follows the Padakalpataru (PK) and the Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

1. Madhavi Dasa — "kalaha kariyā chhalā…" (PK 2239)

Lila: the arrival in Puri (1510). Making a quarrel His pretext, the Lord goes on ahead to Jagannatha; Nityananda and the devotees follow His footprints; at the Lion Gate Nitai questions the people of Nilachala; the Lord enters the house of the Bhattacharya (Sarvabhauma). Raga varadi (PK), suhai (GPT).1

কলহ করিয়া ছলা আগে পহু চলি গেলা
ভেটিবারে নীলাচল-রায় ।
যতেক ভকতগণ হৈয়া সকরুণ-মন
পদ-চিহ্ন-অনুসারে ধায় ॥

kalaha kariyā chalā āge pahu cali gelā
bheṭibāre nīlācala-rāya |
yateka bhakatagaṇa haiyā sakaruṇa-mana
pada-cihna-anusāre dhāya ||

kalaha kariya chhala — making a quarrel the pretext; age pahu chali gela — the Lord went on ahead; bhetibare nilachala-raya — to meet the Lord of Nilachala; yateka bhakatagana — all the devotees; haiya sakaruna-mana — their hearts full of grief; pada-chihna-anusare — following the footprints; dhaya — run

1.1Making a quarrel His pretext, the Lord went on ahead
to see the Lord of Nilachala.
All the devotees, their hearts full of grief,
run after Him, following His footprints.2

নিতাই বিরহ-অনলে ভেল ধন্দ ।
আঠারনালাতে হৈতে কান্দিতে কান্দিতে পথে
যায় নিতাই অবধৌত-চন্দ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

nitāi biraha-anale bhela dhanda |
āṭhāranālāte haite kāndite kāndite pathe
yāya nitāi abadhauta-canda || dhru ||

nitai — Nitai; biraha-anale — in the fire of separation; bhela dhanda — became bewildered; atharanala-te haite — from Atharanala; kandite kandite pathe — weeping and weeping on the road; yaya nitai — goes Nitai; abadhauta-chanda — the moon of avadhutas

1.2(Refrain) Nitai, in the fire of separation, is as if in a daze.
From Atharanala, weeping and weeping on the road,
goes Nitai, the moon of avadhutas.3

সিংহ-দুয়ারে গিয়া মরমে বেদনা পাইয়া
দাঁড়াইল নিত্যানন্দ রায় ।
হরে কৃষ্ণ হরি বলে দেখিয়াছ সন্ন্যাসীরে
নীলাচল-বাসীরে সোধায় ॥

siṃha-duyāre giyā marame bedanā pāiyā
dām̐ṛāila nityānanda rāya |
hare kṛṣṇa hari bale dekhiyācha sannyāsīre
nīlācala-bāsīre sodhāya ||

simha-duyare giya — coming to the Lion Gate; marame bedana paiya — with pain in his heart; daraila nityananda raya — Nityananda Raya stopped; hare krishna hari bale — crying "Hare Krishna, Hari!"; dekhiyachha sannyasire — "have you seen a sannyasi?"; nilachala-basire sodhaya — he asks the people of Nilachala

1.3Coming to the Lion Gate, with pain in His heart,
Nityananda Raya stopped.
Crying "Hare Krishna, Hari!" He asks the people of Nilachala:
"Have you seen a sannyasi?

জাম্বুনদ-হেম জিনি গৌর-বরণ-খানি
অরুণ বসন শোভে গায় ।
প্রেম-ভরে গরগর আঁখিযুগ ঝর ঝর
হরি হরি বোল বলি ধায় ॥

jāmbunada-hema jini gaura-baraṇa-khāni
aruṇa basana śobhe gāya |
prema-bhare garagara ām̐khiyuga jhara jhara
hari hari bola bali dhāya ||

jambunada-hema jini — surpassing the gold of the Jambu river; gaura-barana-khani — His golden form; aruna basana shobhe gaya — a red cloth shines on His body; prema-bhare garagara — brimming with prema; ankhi-yuga jhara jhara — tears stream from both eyes; hari hari bola boli dhaya — He runs, crying "Hari, Hari!"

1.4His golden form surpasses the gold of the Jambu river,
a red cloth shines on His body;
brimming with prema, He sheds tears from both eyes
and runs, crying 'Hari, Hari!'"4

ছাড়ি নাগরালি-বেশে ভ্রমে পহু দেশে দেশে
এবে ভেল সন্ন্যাসীর বেশ ।
মাধবী দাসেতে কয় অপরূপ গোরা রায়
ভট্ট-গৃহে করল প্রবেশ ॥

chāṛi nāgarāli-beśe bhrame pahu deśe deśe
ebe bhela sannyāsīra beśa |
mādhabī dāsete kaya aparūpa gorā rāya
bhaṭṭa-gṛhe karala prabeśa ||

chhari nagarali-beshe — leaving the dress of a nagara; bhrame pahu deshe deshe — the Lord wanders from land to land; ebe bhela sannyasira besha — now [He wears] the garb of a sannyasi; madhavi dasete kaya — Madhavi Dasa says; aparupa gora raya — the wondrous Gora Raya; bhatta-grihe karala prabesha — entered the house of the Bhattacharya

1.5Leaving the dress of a nagara, the Lord wanders from land to land —
now He wears the garb of a sannyasi.
Madhavi Dasa says: the wondrous Gora Raya
has entered the house of the Bhattacharya.5

him among the contemporaries; some identify the poet with Madhavi Devi of Puri, the sister of Shikhi Mahiti, whom the Lord counted among Radha's closest maidservants (CC Antya 2), but there is no proof — the attribution is doubtful. GPT1 and GPT2 give the same pada with different readings in almost every line and with another ending — the signature of Govinda Dasa ("Govinda Dasa says: I saw His entry into Sarvabhauma's house"). In PK the pada opens the 21st pallava ("The sannyasa of Sri Gauranga, etc."). The events: CC Madhya 5–6; CB Antya 2; Murari 3.10–3.11; Lochana, Shesha-khanda. Lord, as if angered, went on ahead alone. The poet calls the quarrel a "pretext": the Lord Himself wished to come first to Jagannatha (and to Sarvabhauma). learned that His staff had been broken and went on ahead alone. An avadhuta is a wanderer above outward rules; so Nityananda is called. sannyasi. According to CC (Madhya 6), on seeing Jagannatha the Lord fell senseless in the temple, and Sarvabhauma had Him carried to his house; when Nityananda and the companions came to the Lion Gate, people told them of the sannyasi who had been taken to the Bhattacharya's. "Nagarali" is the manner and dress of a nagara (an elegant young townsman): a hint at the Lord's Navadvipa form as it is sung by the poets of nagari-bhava. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation the Lord did not so much as glance at another man's wife; the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta) does not accept the worship of Gaura in the spirit of "Gaura-nagari".

2. Madhavi — "nityānanda saṅgati mukunda gadādhare…" (PK 2240)

Lila: the sequel to the previous pada — the companions find the Lord in Sarvabhauma's house; the people of Nilachala gaze at Him. Raga — the same (varadi).6

নিত্যানন্দ সঙ্গতি মুকুন্দ গদাধরে ।
দেখিলেন গৌরচন্দ্র সার্ব্বভৌম-ঘরে ॥

nityānanda saṅgati mukunda gadādhare |
dekhilena gauracandra sārvvabhauma-ghare ||

nityananda sangati — together with Nityananda; mukunda gadadhare — Mukunda and Gadadhara; dekhilena gaurachandra — beheld Gaurachandra; sarvabhauma-ghare — in Sarvabhauma's house

2.1Together with Nityananda, Mukunda and Gadadhara
beheld Gaurachandra in Sarvabhauma's house.

প্রতপ্ত কাঞ্চন-কান্তি অরুণ বসন ।
প্রেমে ছল ছল দুই অরুণ নয়ন ॥

pratapta kāñcana-kānti aruṇa basana |
preme chala chala dui aruṇa nayana ||

pratapta kanchana-kanti — the lustre of molten gold; aruna basana — a red cloth; preme chhala chhala — brimming with tears of prema; dui aruna nayana — two reddish eyes

2.2His lustre is like molten gold, His cloth is red;
His two reddish eyes brim with tears of prema.

আজানুলম্বিত ভুজ চন্দনে ভূষিত ।
উন্নত নাসিকা ঊর্দ্ধ-তিলক-শোভিত ॥

ājānulambita bhuja candane bhūṣita |
unnata nāsikā ūrddha-tilaka-śobhita ||

ajanulambita bhuja — arms reaching to the knees; chandane bhushita — adorned with sandal; unnata nasika — a high nose; urdhva-tilaka-shobhita — graced with the urdhva-tilaka

2.3His arms reach to His knees, adorned with sandal;
His nose is high, His brow graced with the urdhva-tilaka.

গোপীনাথ বাণীনাথ সার্ব্বভৌম কাশী ।
গোরা-রূপ দেখে যত নীলাচল-বাসী ॥

gopīnātha bāṇīnātha sārvvabhauma kāśī |
gorā-rūpa dekhe yata nīlācala-bāsī ||

gopinatha — Gopinatha [Acharya]; vaninatha — Vaninatha; sarvabhauma — Sarvabhauma; kashi — Kashi [Mishra]; gora-rupa dekhe — gaze at Gora's form; yata nilachala-basi — all the people of Nilachala

2.4Gopinatha, Vaninatha, Sarvabhauma, Kashi —
all the people of Nilachala gaze at Gora's form.7

দক্ষিণে নিতাই বসি বামে গদাধর ।
মিলিলেন গোরাচাঁদের যত অনুচর ॥

dakṣiṇe nitāi basi bāme gadādhara |
mililena gorācām̐dera yata anucara ||

dakshine nitai basi — on the right sits Nitai; bame gadadhara — on the left Gadadhara; mililena — have gathered; gorachandera yata anuchara — all the followers of Gorachand

2.5Nitai sits on the right, Gadadhara on the left:
all the followers of Gorachand have gathered.

যে দেখয়ে গোরা-মুখ সেই প্রেমে ভাসে ।
মাধবি বঞ্চিত হৈল নিজ কর্ম্ম-দোষে ॥

ye dekhaye gorā-mukha sei preme bhāse |
mādhabi bañcita haila nija karmma-doṣe ||

ye dekhaye gora-mukha — whoever sees Gora's face; sei preme bhase — floats in prema; madhavi banchita haila — Madhavi was left out; nija karma-doshe — through the fault of [Madhavi's] own deeds

2.6Whoever sees Gora's face floats in prema;
Madhavi alone is left out — through the fault of Madhavi's own deeds.8

pada follows the pada on Sarvabhauma seeing the Lord's forms. Cf. CC Madhya 6: Nityananda, Mukunda, Gadadhara (and Jagadananda) come to Sarvabhauma's house, where the Lord lies senseless. Raya was the brother of Ramananda Raya; Kashi is evidently Kashi Mishra, in whose house the Lord later lived. According to CC (Madhya 10), the Lord met Vaninatha and Kashi Mishra after His return from the South; the poet gathers them into a single scene.

3. Narahari (Sarakara) — "dekhi gorā nīlāchala-nātha…" (PK 799)

Lila: the darshan of Jagannatha — the Lord, in a gopi's mood, reproaches Krishna. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "reproaches to Krishna" (akshepanuraga). According to Majumdar, an eyewitness description unequalled in literature. Raga suhai.9

দেখি গোরা নীলাচল-নাথ ।
নিজ পারিষদগণ সাথ ॥

dekhi gorā nīlācala-nātha |
nija pāriṣadagaṇa sātha ||

dekhi — seeing; gora — Gora; nilachala-natha — the Lord of Nilachala; nija parishada-gana satha — with His own associates

3.1Seeing the Lord of Nilachala,
Gora, together with His own associates,

বিভোর হইলা গোপী-ভাবে ।
কহে পহু করিয়া আক্ষেপে ॥

bibhora hailā gopī-bhābe |
kahe pahu kariyā ākṣepe ||

bibhora haila — was overwhelmed; gopi-bhabe — by a gopi's mood; kahe pahu — the Lord says; kariya akshepe — reproachfully

3.2was overwhelmed by a gopi's mood,
and, reproaching, the Lord says:

আমি তোমা না দেখিলে মরি ।
উলটি না চাহ তুমি ফিরি ॥

āmi tomā nā dekhile mari |
ulaṭi nā cāha tumi phiri ||

ami toma na dekhile mari — I perish without seeing You (I cannot live without You); ulati na chaha tumi phiri — yet You do not turn round to look

3.3"Without You I cannot live,
yet You will not even turn round to look at Me!

করিলা পিরিতিময় ফাঁদ ।
হাতে দিলা আকাশের চাঁদ ॥

karilā piritimaya phām̐da |
hāte dilā ākāśera cām̐da ||

karila piritimaya phanda — You set a snare made of love; hate dila akashera chanda — You put the moon of the sky into my hands

3.4You wove a snare of love —
You put the moon of the sky into My hands;

এবে তোমা দেখিতে সন্দেশ ।
কহে গোরা করিয়া আবেশ ॥

ebe tomā dekhite sandeśa |
kahe gorā kariyā ābeśa ||

ebe toma dekhite — now to see You; sandesha — [is only] tidings, hearsay; kahe gora — says Gora; kariya abesha — possessed by the mood

3.5and now to see You is only tidings and hearsay," —
so says Gora, overwhelmed by the mood.10

ছলছল অরুণ নয়ান ।
রসরস বিরস বয়ান ॥

chalachala aruṇa nayāna |
rasarasa birasa bayāna ||

chhalachhala — brimming with tears; aruna nayana — the reddish eyes; rasarasa — [once] full of sweetness; birasa bayana — the face has grown wan

3.6His reddish eyes are brimming with tears,
His face, so full of sweetness, has grown wan.

অপরূপ গৌরাঙ্গ-বিলাস ।
কহে কিছু নরহরি দাস ॥

aparūpa gaurāṅga-bilāsa |
kahe kichu narahari dāsa ||

aparupa — wondrous; gauranga-bilasa — Gauranga's play; kahe kichhu — tells a little; narahari dasa — Narahari Dasa

3.7Wondrous is Gauranga's play —
Narahari Dasa has told a little of it.

the Puri padas written in the Lord's lifetime. GPT (GPT1, p. 299, no. 23) has the same pada with minor variants. In Radha's mood the Lord sees Krishna Himself in Jagannatha — cf. CC Madhya 13 (at the Ratha-yatra: "You are the same, I am the same…") and Antya 14 (darshan at the Garuda-stambha). The gopi's reproaches are a manifestation of the highest prema, not of worldly resentment. The sense is the same: the meeting that was once so close has become unattainable.

4. Vasu Ramananda — "nāchaye chaitanya chintāmaṇi…" (PK 2082)

Lila: the Lord dances in the sankirtana. According to Majumdar, Puri: the Lord is called here by His sannyasa name — "Chaitanya". Raga pathamanjari.11

নাচয়ে চৈতন্য চিন্তামণি ।
বুক বাহি পড়ে ধারা মুকুতা-গাঁথুনি ॥ ধ্রু ॥

nācaye caitanya cintāmaṇi |
buka bāhi paṛe dhārā mukutā-gām̐thuni || dhru ||

nachaye — dances; chaitanya — Chaitanya; chintamani — the chintamani gem; buka bahi — flowing down the chest; pare dhara — streams fall; mukuta-ganthuni — [like] strung pearls

4.1(Refrain) Chaitanya dances — the chintamani gem;
streams of tears flow down His chest like strings of pearls.

প্রেমে গদগদ হৈয়া ধরণী লোটায় ।
হুহুঙ্কার দিয়া খেণে উঠিয়া দাঁড়ায় ॥

preme gadagada haiyā dharaṇī loṭāya |
huhuṅkāra diyā kheṇe uṭhiyā dām̐ṛāya ||

preme gadagada haiya — in prema, His voice choked; dharani lotaya — He rolls on the ground; huhunkara diya — with a thundering cry; khene uthiya daraya — suddenly He rises and stands

4.2In prema, His voice choked, He rolls on the ground;
suddenly, with a thundering cry, He rises to His full height.

ঘন ঘন দেন পাক ঊর্দ্ধ বাহু করি ।
পতিত জনারে পহু বোলায় হরি হরি ॥

ghana ghana dena pāka ūrddha bāhu kari |
patita janāre pahu bolāya hari hari ||

ghana ghana dena paka — again and again He whirls; urdhva bahu kari — raising His arms; patita janare — the fallen people; pahu bolaya hari hari — the Lord makes say "Hari, Hari"

4.3Again and again He whirls, arms raised,
and makes the fallen say "Hari, Hari!"12

হরিনাম করে গান জপে অনুক্ষণ ।
বুঝিতে না পারে কেহ বিরল লক্ষণ ॥

harināma kare gāna jape anukṣaṇa |
bujhite nā pāre keha birala lakṣaṇa ||

harinama kare gana — He sings the name of Hari; jape anukshana — repeats it ceaselessly; bujhite na pare keha — no one can understand; birala lakshana — the rare signs

4.4He sings the name of Hari, ceaselessly repeating it —
no one can fathom these rare signs.

অপার মহিমা গুণ জগ-জনে গায় ।
বসু রামানন্দে তাহে প্রেম-ধন চায় ॥

apāra mahimā guṇa jaga-jane gāya |
basu rāmānande tāhe prema-dhana cāya ||

apara mahima guna — boundless glory and virtues; jaga-jane gaya — the people of the world sing; basu ramanande — Vasu Ramananda; tahe — of Him; prema-dhana chaya — begs the treasure of prema

4.5His boundless glory and virtues the whole world sings;
Vasu Ramananda begs Him for the treasure of prema.

the Lord charged the people of Kulinagrama — Satyaraja Khan and Ramananda Vasu — to bring silk ropes every year for the Ratha-yatra. Majumdar regards him as a contemporary and an eyewitness. In GPT2 the pada is given twice (the section "dance and kirtana", nos. 17 and 74); in the second instance the first couplet is marked as the refrain. Cf. CC Madhya 11, 13 (the Lord's kirtanas in Puri). without distinction.

5. Narahari (Sarakara) — "tribhubana-manohara śachīra nandana mora…" (PK 2241)

Lila: from the sannyasa to Nilachala — the Lord leaves His former appearance and gives away the holy name and prema; sankirtana on the seashore with Svarupa, Rupa, Ramananda, Govinda and Paramananda Puri. According to Majumdar, a pada by an eyewitness of the Puri period. Raga bhatiyari.13

ত্রিভুবন-মনোহর শচীর নন্দন মোর
নদীয়া নগরে যার বাস ।
সকল সম্পদ ছাড়ি সন্ন্যাস গ্রহণ করি
নীলাচলে জগন্নাথ পাশ ॥

tribhubana-manohara śacīra nandana mora
nadīyā nagare yāra bāsa |
sakala sampada chāṛi sannyāsa grahaṇa kari
nīlācale jagannātha pāśa ||

tribhubana-manohara — enchanter of the three worlds; shachira nandana mora — Shachi's son, my [Lord]; nadiya nagare yara basa — who lived in the town of Nadia; sakala sampada chhari — leaving all wealth; sannyasa grahana kari — taking sannyasa; nilachale jagannatha pasha — in Nilachala, near Jagannatha

5.1The enchanter of the three worlds, Shachi's son, my Lord,
who lived in the town of Nadia,
gave up all His wealth and took sannyasa —
and He is in Nilachala, near Jagannatha.

যে চাঁচর কেশ দেখি মোহ যায় রতি-পতি
মুণ্ডন করিল হেন কেশ ।
কনক অঙ্গদ বালা মণি মুকুতার মালা
তেয়াগিলা সে মোহন বেশ ॥

ye cām̐cara keśa dekhi moha yāya rati-pati
muṇḍana karila hena keśa |
